title: Plotting energyRt objects
text: example calendars dataset holds ready-made calendar objects. autoplot() (equivalent plot()) draws timeframe row rectangles sized timeslice’s share year:
code: data("calendars", package = "energyRt") names(calendars) #>  [1] "annual"                 "d365"                   "d365_h24"               #>  [4] "m12"                    "m12a"                   "q4"                     #>  [7] "s4"                     "s4_h24"                 "m12_h24"                #> [10] "wd7_h24"                "w52_h24"                "s4_h24_subset_2seasons" #> [13] "m12_h24_subset_4months" "m12_subset_q1"          "d365_h24_1dps"          #> [16] "d365_h24_1dpm"          "s4_hp3"                 "m12_d365_h24"           #> [19] "m12_d365_h24_1dpm" autoplot(calendars$s4_hp3)

title: Plotting energyRt objects
text: fill = "order" (default) color_pattern controls gradient. "within" (default) colours level timeslices — hourly row shows full h00→h23 cycle repeating every day, "global" colours absolute chronology across whole year.   fill metrics timeslice "share" "weight":
code: autoplot(calendars$d365_h24)                          # within (default) autoplot(calendars$d365_h24, color_pattern = "global") autoplot(calendars$s4_hp3, fill = "share")

title: Plotting energyRt objects
text: cell can labelled individual level name ("name", default, e.g. h00…h23) full timeslice path ("timeslice", e.g. d001_h00). Label text auto-contrasts fill; override label_color.
code: # zoom (see below) so labels are legible autoplot(calendars$d365_h24,          show_leafs = list(YDAY = "d001", HOUR = 1:24),          label_by = "name")

title: Plotting energyRt objects
text: show_leafs selects timeslices draw. Pass named list filter per timeframe level (character = timeslice names, numeric = positions among level’s timeslices), unnamed vector filter finest level directly.
code: # day 100, hours 5-10 autoplot(calendars$d365_h24, show_leafs = list(YDAY = "d100", HOUR = 5:10)) # the first 48 leaf timeslices (first two days) autoplot(calendars$d365_h24, show_leafs = 1:48)

title: Plotting energyRt objects
text: reduced calendar can shown full reference calendar: pass full one reference. timeslices present subset filled; rest left empty.
code: autoplot(calendars$d365_h24_1dpm,          reference = calendars$d365_h24)

title: Plotting energyRt objects
text: autoplot() lays every timeslice one row per timeframe. value indexed two-dimensional calendar — day--year × hour, month × hour — heatmap reads naturally: plot_heatmap() puts finest timeframe y, next x, coarser levels facets. layout taken calendar, pass calendar = – either calendar object name one, "d365_h24". synthetic hourly load profile d365_h24 calendar (daily cycle plus seasonal swing). diurnal band winter/summer contrast immediately visible:  Facet day--year format "month" get one day--month × hour panel per month:  palette selects viridis option name labels colour bar, exactly autoplot().
code: cal  <- calendars$d365_h24 tt   <- cal@timetable prof <- data.frame(   timeslice = tt$timeslice,   load  = 50 + 30 * sin(2 * pi * (timescales::tsl2hour(tt$timeslice, cal@name) - 6) / 24) +                 15 * cos(2 * pi *  timescales::tsl2yday(tt$timeslice, cal@name)      / 365))  plot_heatmap(prof, calendar = cal, value = "load")   # x = YDAY, y = HOUR plot_heatmap(prof, calendar = cal, value = "load", facet = "month")  # 12 panels

title: Plotting energyRt objects
text: timeslice-indexed model data lays way. electricity demand solar capacity factor packaged TOPIA kit, season × hour calendar (s4_h24): pull object getObject(), take one region (, demand, one year), pass timeslice + value columns plot_heatmap(). name argument carries value’s unit onto colour bar.   weather heatmap exactly autoplot() draws weather object directly — line area variants (see Weather ).
code: repo <- topia$modules$electricity$R3$repo wcal <- calendars$s4_h24  DEM <- getObject(repo, name = "DEM_ELC", drop = TRUE) dem <- subset(as.data.frame(DEM@demand), region == "W1" & year == 2050) plot_heatmap(dem[, c("timeslice", "demand")], calendar = wcal, value = "demand",              name = "PJ") WSOL <- getObject(repo, name = "WSOL", drop = TRUE) wsol <- subset(as.data.frame(WSOL@weather), region == "W1") plot_heatmap(wsol[, c("timeslice", "wval")], calendar = wcal, value = "wval",              name = "capacity factor")

title: Solver backends and solver_options
text: solver_options named list ready-made presets — one pins backend, solver, data-exchange format, solver-specific tuning: Use preset one two ways: set_default_solver() lasts session. make default stick across sessions, save en_config_write(); en_config_show() reports current default together solver paths depends . solve_model() interpolates model solves ; solve_scenario() solves already-interpolated scenario. solver = NULL scenario’s settings get_default_solver() used.
code: names(solver_options) solver_options$glpk solver_options$julia_highs_barrier # 1. Set it as the session default, then solve normally set_default_solver(solver_options$julia_highs) get_default_solver()                       # inspect the current default scen <- solve_model(model)                   # uses the default  # 2. Pass it explicitly to a single solve scen <- solve_model(model,  solver = solver_options$glpk) scen <- solve_scenario(scen,  solver = solver_options$gams_gdx_cplex)

title: Solver backends and solver_options
text: GNU Linear Programming Kit. energyRt writes model GMPL/MathProg calls glpsol executable — lowest-friction option good default small medium models.
code: solve_model(model, solver = solver_options$glpk)

title: Solver backends and solver_options
text: energyRt writes Pyomo ConcreteModel solves configured solver. CBC open-source default; CPLEX GLPK also available. Model data solution exchanged Arrow files, needs pyarrow Python environment (en_install_python_deps() installs ); solver_options$pyomo_cbc_sqlite selects older SQLite exchange instead.
code: solve_model(model, solver = solver_options$pyomo_cbc) solve_model(model, solver = solver_options$pyomo_cplex_barrier)   # CPLEX barrier

title: Solver backends and solver_options
text: energyRt writes JuMP model solves Julia. HiGHS (open-source) fast recommended choice large models; *_barrier, *_simplex *_parallel presets select HiGHS algorithm. Cbc, GLPK CPLEX also available. Model data solution exchanged Arrow files, read written Arrow.jl (en_install_julia_pkgs() installs ); solver_options$julia_highs_rdata selects older RData exchange instead.
code: solve_model(model, solver = solver_options$julia_highs)           # default (auto) solve_model(model, solver = solver_options$julia_highs_barrier)   # interior point solve_model(model, solver = solver_options$julia_highs_parallel)  # parallel simplex

title: Solver backends and solver_options
text: Linux . cuOpt solves JuMP model NVIDIA GPU cuOpt.jl. ships Windows build, Windows Julia process must run inside WSL. Install cuOpt first (pip install --extra-index-url=https://pypi.nvidia.com cuopt-cu12), put libcuopt.LD_LIBRARY_PATH, add wrapper en_install_julia_pkgs("cuOpt"). cuOpt.jl supports one cuOpt release time, installed cuopt-cu12 must match . method selects algorithm: 0 races PDLP barrier GPU dual simplex CPU returns whichever finishes first, 1 PDLP alone. preset use follows solution consumed: julia_cuopt_pdlp – PDLP never factorizes, GPU memory grows linearly non-zeros. preset models whose barrier factorization fit GPU memory. solution carries duality gap 1e-4, fine capacities dispatch prices. julia_cuopt_crossover – adds crossover basic solution, duals (therefore shadow prices) require. Costs little extra time recovers exact optimum. julia_cuopt_concurrent – fastest small medium models, barrier leg dominates GPU memory winning algorithm can differ runs, model may return byte-identical results twice.
code: solve_model(model, solver = solver_options$julia_cuopt_pdlp)      # first-order, GPU solve_model(model, solver = solver_options$julia_cuopt_crossover) # + basic solution solve_model(model, solver = solver_options$julia_cuopt_concurrent)# race all three

title: Solver backends and solver_options
text: GAMS license, energyRt can write run GAMS model. gams_gdx_* presets exchange data GDX (fast, native); gams_csv_* presets use text/CSV. *_barrier *_parallel presets inject tuned cplex.opt (LP method, threads, crossover, …).
code: solve_model(model, solver = solver_options$gams_gdx_cplex) solve_model(model, solver = solver_options$gams_gdx_cplex_barrier)

title: Solver backends and solver_options
text: NEOS Server runs commercial solvers (CPLEX, …) free internet. model built locally solve dispatched NEOS, can use CPLEX without local license. Two families provided — via Pyomo (neos_pyomo_*) via GAMS (neos_gams_*, sent inlined text local GAMS install needed). NEOS requires email address, set via NEOS_EMAIL environment variable helper (one energyRt setting whose environment variable prefixed ENERGYRT_, Pyomo subprocess reads NEOS_EMAIL directly): low-level NEOS interface (submit/poll/fetch job, list solvers, …) also exported — see ?neos neos_* functions.
code: set_neos_email("you@example.org") solve_model(model, solver = solver_options$neos_gams_cplex) solve_model(model, solver = solver_options$neos_pyomo_cplex_barrier)

title: Get started with energyRt
text: first model one fuel, one power plant, one electricity demand. units timeframe explicit: annual energy measured PJ, capacity GW, costs MEUR.  Collect bricks, define planning horizon, bind model one region, solve bundled GLPK solver: solve_model() interpolates solves one call. composable form exposes intermediate scenario needs inspected modified: Results return tables level detail model: model built 1.59 GW gas capacity—enough supply 50 PJ per year declared conversion efficiency. solved scenario also contains every underlying flow, cost, balance.
code: GAS <- newCommodity(   name = "GAS",   desc = "Natural gas",   timeframe = "ANNUAL",   unit = "PJ" ) ELC <- newCommodity(   name = "ELC",   desc = "Electricity",   timeframe = "ANNUAL",   unit = "PJ" )  gas_supply <- data.frame(   cost = 6.0 ) SUP_GAS <- newSupply(   name = "SUP_GAS",   desc = "Natural gas supply",   commodity = "GAS",   unit = "PJ",   supply = gas_supply )  gas_efficiency <- data.frame(   comm = "GAS",   cinp2use = 0.55 ) gas_investment <- data.frame(   invcost = 900 ) EGAS <- newTechnology(   name = "EGAS",   desc = "Combined-cycle gas power plant",   input = list(comm = "GAS"),   output = list(comm = "ELC"),   ceff = gas_efficiency,   invcost = gas_investment,   fixom = 25,   cap2act = 31.536,   olife = 25L )  electricity_demand <- data.frame(   demand = 50 ) DEM_ELC <- newDemand(   name = "DEM_ELC",   desc = "Annual electricity demand",   commodity = "ELC",   unit = "PJ",   demand = electricity_demand )  draw(object = EGAS) HELLO_REPOSITORY <- newRepository(   name = "HELLO_REPOSITORY",   GAS,   ELC,   SUP_GAS,   EGAS,   DEM_ELC,   desc = "Components of the introductory electricity model" )  HELLO_HORIZON <- newHorizon(   name = "HELLO_HORIZON",   desc = "Planning horizon from 2025 through 2040",   period = 2025:2040,   intervals = c(1, 5, 10),   mid_is_end = TRUE )  HELLO <- newModel(   name = "HELLO",   desc = "Single-region gas-to-electricity model",   data = HELLO_REPOSITORY,   region = "R1",   discount = 0.05,   horizon = HELLO_HORIZON )  BASE <- solve_model(   object = HELLO,   name = "BASE",   solver = solver_options$glpk,   echo = FALSE ) BASE_STAGED <- HELLO |>   interpolate(name = "BASE_STAGED") |>   solve() base_objective <- getData(   object = BASE,   name = "vObjective",   merge = TRUE ) base_capacity <- getData(   object = BASE,   name = "vTechCap",   merge = TRUE )  base_objective #> # A tibble: 1 × 3 #>   scenario name       value #>   <chr>    <chr>      <dbl> #> 1 BASE     vObjective 6677. base_capacity #> # A tibble: 3 × 6 #>   scenario name     tech  region  year value #>   <chr>    <chr>    <chr> <chr>  <int> <dbl> #> 1 BASE     vTechCap EGAS  R1      2025  1.59 #> 2 BASE     vTechCap EGAS  R1      2030  1.59 #> 3 BASE     vTechCap EGAS  R1      2040  1.59

title: Get started with energyRt
text: Sampling changes temporal representation scenario. useful rapid exploration, approximation unless chosen slices representative. sample must retain complete members calendar level; calendar_samples() builds valid sample specifications records much year one covers. solve_by_sample() interpolates solves sample, preserving sample definition runs. larger TOPIA example executed introductory vignette builds: See Time resolution Workflow manual calendar subsets, weighting, repeated samples, comparisons full solve.
code: data(   list = "topia",   package = "energyRt" ) s4_h24 <- topia$modules$calendars$s4_h24  SEASON_SAMPLES <- calendar_samples(   calendar = s4_h24,   level = "SEASON",   sample_size = 2,   n = 2,   method = "random",   seed = 2050 ) SEASON_SAMPLES #> calendar_samples: 2 sample(s), method = random #>   slices per sample: 48-48 | distinct slices used: 96 TOPIA_KIT <- topia$modules$electricity$R1 TOPIA_SAMPLING <- newModel(   name = "TOPIA_SAMPLING",   desc = "TOPIA model used to demonstrate calendar sampling",   data = TOPIA_KIT$repo,   calendar = s4_h24,   region = TOPIA_KIT$regions,   horizon = topia$modules$horizons$base,   discount = 0.05 ) TOPIA_SAMPLING <- setGeoscale(   obj = TOPIA_SAMPLING,   geoscale = TOPIA_KIT$geoscale )  TOPIA_SAMPLES <- solve_by_sample(   object = TOPIA_SAMPLING,   name = "TOPIA_SAMPLES",   samples = SEASON_SAMPLES,   solver = solver_options$glpk,   echo = FALSE,   verbose = FALSE ) sample_summary(   x = TOPIA_SAMPLES,   name = "vTechCap",   by = "tech" )

title: Features
text: Component classes. commodity, supply, demand, technology, storage, trade, weather, constraint, tax, subsidy, costs, plus import / export flows across model boundary. built newX() constructor, carries data slots, edited update(), derives variant instead re-typing object. Technologies convert number input commodities number outputs, conversion given per commodity (ceff), per group commodities (@group), process activity (cap2act); availability timeslice (af), summed slices (afs) per commodity (afc); ramping limits; capacity retirement bounds; investment, fixed variable costs. Auxiliary flows (@aux / @aeff) couple process’s capacity, new capacity, retirement, activity flows commodity — land per MW, water per MWh, emission per unit fuel. sit auxiliary commodity’s timeframe, annual emission hourly plant one variable per year. Storage three parts — charger, reservoir, discharger — capacity variable (vStorageInpCap, vStorageStgCap, vStorageOutCap), costs availability. @duration sets reservoir hours per unit discharge power, @inp2out charger/discharger ratio @inp2stg charging C-rate; @seff holds charge, discharge self-discharge efficiency; @startLevel initial state. storage may store one commodity charge discharge another. Trade carries commodity regions declared routes, efficiency, capacity, costs, availability lifetime. newACLine() newDCLink() wrap two common electrical cases; lossTranches() approximates quadratic losses capacity tranches; opt-Kirchhoff voltage law constrains loop flows. Weather supplies exogenous time series multiplies process’s availability — capacity factors, inflows, charging window. One series can serve many processes, declared coarser region users, derive series registered transforms (register_weather_transform()). Policy objects. constraint writes arbitrary linear restriction declared summands; tax subsidy levy commodity total named process; costs adds user-defined cost term objective. Commodity properties. @property carries physical data (heating values, densities, carbon content) tidy table; @emis emission factors; @agg aggregation reporting groups; @limtype balance direction. Units declared flows capacities, cap2act making capacity--activity conversion explicit, getUnits() reporting model carries. Portable definitions. process_to_spec() / process_from_spec() write read process YAML JSON; process_spec_issues() lints one; process_designer() interactive Shiny editor; read_technology_xlsx() / write_technology_xlsx() round-trip Excel.

code: source("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/optimal2050/energyRt/master/inst/install.R") install_energyRt() install_energyRt(branch = "dev") install.packages("pak") pak::pkg_install("optimal2050/energyRt")  # or, with remotes: # install.packages("remotes") # remotes::install_github("optimal2050/energyRt") install.packages("pak")  # energyRt's direct CRAN imports (base packages are omitted): deps <- c(   "generics", "data.table", "DBI", "RSQLite", "tibble", "tidyr", "dplyr",   "rlang", "stringr", "lubridate", "purrr", "arrow", "progressr", "tictoc",   "cli", "zoo", "registry", "options", "glue", "plyr",   # suggested — plots and reports (optional but recommended, see section 7):   "ggplot2", "patchwork", "knitr", "rmarkdown", "tinytex", "sf" )  failed <- character(0) for (pkg in deps) {   ok <- tryCatch(     {       pak::pkg_install(pkg, ask = FALSE)       message("  [ok]   ", pkg)       TRUE     },     error = function(e) {       message("  [FAIL] ", pkg, ": ", conditionMessage(e))       FALSE     }   )   if (!ok) failed <- c(failed, pkg) }  if (length(failed) == 0) {   message("All dependencies installed — installing energyRt itself:")   pak::pkg_install("optimal2050/energyRt") } else {   message("Failed packages: ", paste(failed, collapse = ", ")) } pak::pkg_sysreqs("optimal2050/energyRt")   # lists the apt packages # e.g. sudo apt install libcurl4-openssl-dev libssl-dev libxml2-dev

(A technology has one capacity and keeps the bare names.)   aeff = data.frame(acomm = "MAT", out.ncap2ainp = 0.25))  # per new discharge capacity draw(STG_ELC)

title: Model bricks
text: technology converts input commodities output commodities. Read diagram left--right four internal stages: cinp2use — much common use unit commodity input provides (e.g. converting fuels common energy basis). use2cact — use technology’s activity (central variable costs, availability capacity tied ). cact2cout — activity output commodity (efficiency / yield). three default 1.  four column headers box (inp, use, act, ) exactly stages; coefficient printed next flow scales.
code: input(s)  ──▶  use  ──▶  activity  ──▶  output(s)              cinp2use   use2cact      cact2cout BOILER <- newTechnology(   name = "BOILER", desc = "Gas boiler",   input  = data.frame(comm = "GAS",  unit = "PJ"),   output = data.frame(comm = "HEAT", unit = "PJ"),   ceff = data.frame(comm = c("GAS", "HEAT"),                     cinp2use  = c(1,  NA),                     cact2cout = c(NA, 0.9)),   # 90% efficiency   cap2act = 1) draw(BOILER)

title: Model bricks
text: several commodities interchangeable input (output) side, put group. group converted use (via ginp2use geff), member’s contribution bounded share (grp.share.lo/grp.share./grp.share.fx – named GROUP share, since cap.share.fx act.share.* @cluster different things). cinp2ginp converts commodity group’s common unit.  share range drawn square brackets next grouped commodity. Mixed units live coefficients. inputs outputs use different units conversion appear somewhere, use, activity cap2act agree — chain coefficient natural place . fuels PJ electricity GWh: ginp2use = 277.78 converts fuel group GWh (technology operates GWh), cap2act = 8760 matches (1 GW × 8760 h). work factor hand: convert("PJ", "GWh", 1) gives . See Units article unit declared convert() finds factor.
code: CHP <- newTechnology(   name = "CHP", desc = "Co-firing plant (coal + biomass)",   input = data.frame(comm = c("COA", "BIO"), group = "fuel", unit = "PJ"),   output = data.frame(comm = "ELC", unit = "GWh"),   group = data.frame(group = "fuel", desc = "Blended fuel", unit = "PJ"),   # inputs are PJ but the output is GWh: the PJ->GWh conversion (1 PJ =   # 277.78 GWh) rides on `ginp2use`, so use/activity are measured in GWh   geff  = data.frame(group = "fuel", ginp2use = 277.78),   ceff  = data.frame(comm = c("COA", "BIO", "ELC"),                     cinp2ginp = c(1, 1, NA),                     cact2cout = c(NA, NA, 0.4),     # 40% efficiency                     grp.share.up = c(1.0, 0.3, NA)),   # max 30% biomass   cap2act = 8760)                                   # 1 GW x 8760 h = 8760 GWh draw(CHP)

text: Everything technology measured activity. Installed capacity limits maximum activity scalar cap2act: cap2act — “much product (activity, output commodity identical) produced per unit capacity”. units activity per capacity, number depends . power plant rated GW running flat year produces 8760 GWh, cap2act = 8760 activity GWh — cap2act = 31.536 plant activity PJ (1 GW × 8760 h = 31.536 PJ), convention TOPIA uses. Capacity bounded capacity slot: stock (pre-existing), cap.lo//fx (total), ncap.lo//fx (new builds) ret.lo//fx (retirement). Availability factors af/afs bound activity within capacity: af.caps activity timeslice fraction capacity — maximum capacity factor per slice, af.lo must-run floor — afs bounds activity summed timeframe, afs timeslice = "ANNUAL" annual capacity-factor bound (e.g. afs.lo = 0.4 forces least 40% annual utilization). third variant, afc.* ceff slot, applies capacity-relative bound individual commodity flow instead total activity.

title: Model bricks
text: Auxiliary commodities extra flows tracked alongside main conversion — emissions (NOx, SO2, CH4, PM10, PM25), recovered HEAT, land, cooling WATER, construction MATerials, -products. declared aux linked aeff coefficient named <driver>2a<|inp>: driver scales flow: cinp (commodity input), cout (output), act (activity), cap (installed capacity), ncap (new capacity), storage terms; …2aout produces aux commodity (emissions, recovered heat, -products); …2ainp consumes (water, materials, energy). tab isolates one driver base technology (GAS → ELC).
code: aux_tech <- function(param, value, acomm = "AUX", unit = "unit") {   aeff <- data.frame(acomm = acomm, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)   aeff[[param]] <- value   newTechnology(     name = paste0("TECH_", param), desc = paste0("aux via ", param),     input  = data.frame(comm = "GAS", unit = "PJ"),     output = data.frame(comm = "ELC", unit = "GWh"),     ceff   = data.frame(comm = c("GAS", "ELC"), cinp2use = c(1, NA), cact2cout = c(NA, 0.4)),     aux    = data.frame(acomm = acomm, unit = unit),     aeff   = aeff) }

text: Beyond physics baked process, can add linear constraints model variables. newConstraint() low-level form: name raw model variable, dimension (.), relation (eq) right-hand side (rhs). classic use economy-wide emission cap: left-hand term names variable constrains, .sum says members sum — capping new capacity one technology reads: term can also targeted rather enumerated. process_ regular expression process names, vintage cluster select variants vintaged clustered process, classes restricts process class — filters newTax() newSubsidy() take. name .sum matches nothing error, never silent zero, declared (base) name expands realized variants:
code: CO2CAP <- newConstraint(   name = "CO2CAP", desc = "Economy-wide CO2 cap", eq = "<=",   for.each  = data.frame(year = c(2030, 2040, 2050), comm = "CO2"),   emissions = list(variable = "vEmsFuelTot"),         # LHS term   rhs       = data.frame(year = c(2030, 2050), rhs = c(5000, 2000)),   defVal    = Inf) CO2CAP@rhs        # the emission-cap path (interpolated over the horizon) #>   year  rhs #> 1 2030 5000 #> 2 2050 2000 # limit total new coal capacity across the horizon COALLIM <- newConstraint(   name = "COALLIM", desc = "Cap on new coal capacity", eq = "<=",   cap = list(variable = "vTechNewCap", for.sum = list(tech = "PLANT")),   rhs = 50, defVal = 0) COALLIM@lhs[[1]]@for.sum$tech #> [1] "PLANT" # every vintage of ECOA built in 2030, by regex and by vintage newConstraint(   name = "ECOA30", eq = "<=",   cap = list(variable = "vTechCap", process_ = "^ECOA", vintage = "2030"),   for.each = data.frame(year = 2030), rhs = 100, defVal = 0)

title: Reports and levelized costs
text: Container reports split role: report(model) documents assumptions (configuration, inventories, per-process sheets), report(scenario) documents results solved scenario — status, generation/capacity charts, costs, emissions; run = renders recorded run, template = "full" switches comprehensive page-broken layout maps branding. Reporting single process container injects container-priced levelized cost: process sections follow groups: named list process names regular expressions, passed groups = stored mod@misc$report_groups (scenario inherits model’s). Without groups report shows representative sample 12 processes; groups = "topology" groups automatically structure. levcost = TRUE adds levelized-cost comparison — overall chart, one chart per group, ranked table — ex-ante model, ex-post solved scenario; process datasheet requested container also compares process structural peers: Figures reports carry captions rather -plot titles, faceted charts cap 16 panels height following layout. Custom templates get behaviour report_fig(p, width, caption = ). shipped templates listed report_templates(); custom .Rmd templates build exported report_* helper family passed via template = "<path>".

title: Scenario management: how models, scenarios, and solutions are organized
text: scenario one interpolated instance model: model compiled onto concrete calendar, horizon, region scope. Solving — possibly several times, several solvers — produces runs. disk: output/ modOut/ two tiers, copy. output/ solver’s raw dump, backend’s naming types; modOut/ imported store, import real work — normalises backend away (GDX, CSV, Arrow Parquet land one place), synthesises set aliases solver writes, types every dimension declared members, computes vTechEmsFuel vUserCosts, solver ever produced. Re-deriving demand also need @modInp, variant swap may replaced — store answer, cache. See ?read_solution. solution imported, output/ copy , drop_solver_outputs() refuses remove . Three ideas notice: run owns artifacts. Solving scenario second backend overwrite anything: run keeps inputs, raw outputs, provenance, parsed solution. -memory scenario object holds ONE active solution time; switching read, re-solve. run’s location derived. Nothing stores “run X lives” — always <scenario>/runs/<run-id>/, computed demand. moved scenario folder strand runs. default: scenario.yml . names run bare read_solution(scen) resolves loading; save sets active run, may edit file point elsewhere. Let’s produce tree. run = "<label>" names run explicitly; without , label defaults solver directory name (e.g. "glpk"): scenario_run_info(scen, "glpk") returns one run’s full run.yml; read_solution(scen, run = "glpk") switches active solution; drop_scenario_run(scen, "glpk-alt") deletes run (active one force = TRUE). external working directory — outside scenario, run record — available via solve_scenario(solver.dir = "..."), transient = TRUE solves throwaway folder. folder names — <name-model-calendar-horizon> slug, store entry basenames, default solve label — derived built-functions can override set_path_builder() (see toolbox ). Custom names safe nothing ever parsed back folder name: scenarios store entries found name recorded manifests registry. run tree (runs/<variant>/<solve>/) structural overridable.
code: scenarios/<name-model-calendar-horizon>/ ├── scenario.yml        # manifest: model reference, calendar, horizon, │                       #   `default:` — the default run (edit it freely) ├── scen.RData          # the thin S4 shell (all big data lives beside it) ├── class · format · layout · logfile.csv ├── modInp/parameters/<param>/           # the (base) interpolated problem ├── modOut/variables/<var>/              # the scenario's own solution, once │                       #   promoted — with modOut.yml recording which run │                       #   produced it (see "A solution of its own") ├── model/…             # the model's data — only when embedded (see below) └── runs/               # one folder per solver run     ├── glpk/                            # a base-problem run     │   ├── run.yml     #   provenance: solver, cmdline, started/finished,     │   │               #   duration, status, objective, host, user     │   ├── input/      #   the exchange tables handed to the solver     │   ├── output/     #   the solver's raw dump; read_solution() reads it     │   └── modOut/variables/<var>/      #   the parsed solution store     └── julia_highs/…                    # another backend, side by side scen <- interpolate_model(mod, name = "BASE") |>   solve_scenario(solver = solver_options$glpk, echo = FALSE) scen <- solve_scenario(scen, solver = solver_options$glpk, echo = FALSE,                    force = TRUE, run = "glpk-alt") scenario_runs(scen)[, c("run", "status", "solver_name", "objective", "active")] #> # A tibble: 2 × 5 #>   run      status solver_name objective active #>   <chr>    <chr>  <chr>           <dbl> <lgl>  #> 1 glpk     solved glpk              300 FALSE  #> 2 glpk-alt solved glpk              300 TRUE scen <- save_scenario(scen, verbose = FALSE) #> Scenario 'BASE' saved in 'C:/Users/admin/AppData/Local/Temp/Rtmp639Dbr/sm-demo/scenarios/BASE-SM-smc' #> Directory size: 0.39 MB sort(list.files(scen@path)) #> [1] "class"        "format"       "layout"       "logfile.csv"  "runs"         #> [6] "scen.RData"   "scenario.yml"

title: TOPIA I: building the model
text: Electricity demand follows deterministic load shape, weighted timeslice’s share year grown milestone years. Two views demand object: aggregated annual totals region (type = "area", default), within-year profiles region year (type = "line") – note morning ramp evening peak:
code: years  <- c(2025, 2030, 2040, 2050) growth <- c(1, 1.2, 1.4, 1.6) annual_demand <- 100                                   # base-year PJ per region  share <- as.data.frame(cal@timeslice_share)[, c("timeslice", "share")] d0 <- merge(prof$demand, share, by = "timeslice") d0$w <- d0$load * d0$share dem_rows <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(years), function(i) {   do.call(rbind, lapply(regions, function(r) {     dr <- d0[d0$region == r, ]     data.frame(region = r, year = years[i], timeslice = dr$timeslice,                demand = annual_demand * growth[i] * dr$w / sum(dr$w))   })) }))  DEM_ELC <- newDemand(   name = "DEM_ELC",   desc = "Final electricity demand",   commodity = "ELC",   unit = "PJ",   demand = dem_rows ) autoplot(DEM_ELC, years = 2025:2055) # autoplot(DEM_ELC, style = "line", years = c(2025, 2050)) # autoplot(DEM_ELC, style = "heatmap", years = c(2025, 2050))

title: TOPIA I: building the model
text: Policies pathways pre-built objects layered onto base model running scenarios (mirroring IDEEA’s CO2_CAP etc.): CO2_CAP – declining cap CO2 emissions (newConstraint vEmsFuelTot; starts near BASE emissions (~5,000 kt/region 2025) tightens deep cut 2050); CT_CO2 – rising carbon tax (newTax; costs MUSD emissions kt, 20-80 USD/t reads 0.02-0.08 MUSD/kt – watch units); RES_SHARE – growing renewable-generation floor; NO_NEW_NUC – new nuclear capacity; EARLY_RET – forced early retirement coal gas fleets (declining per-region ceiling installed coal gas capacity; optimizeRetirement = TRUE plants lets model choose units close).
code: nreg <- length(regions) CO2_CAP <- newConstraint(   name = "CO2_CAP",   eq = "<=",   for.each = data.frame(year = years, comm = "CO2"),   term1 = list(variable = "vEmsFuelTot"),   rhs = data.frame(year = range(years), rhs = c(5000, 2500) * nreg),   defVal = Inf )  CT_CO2 <- newTax(   name = "CT_CO2",   comm = "CO2",   tax = data.frame(year = range(years), bal = c(0.02, 0.08))  # 20-80 USD/t )  ren <- c("ESOL", "EWIN", "EHYD") sh  <- seq(0.15, 0.50, length.out = length(years)) RES_SHARE <- newConstraint(   name = "RES_SHARE",   eq = ">=",   for.each = data.frame(year = years, comm = "ELC"),   term1 = list(variable = "vTechOut", for.sum = list(tech = ren)),   rhs = data.frame(year = years, rhs = sh * annual_demand * growth * nreg),   defVal = 0 )  NO_NEW_NUC <- newConstraint(   name = "NO_NEW_NUC",   eq = "<=",   for.each = data.frame(year = years, tech = "ENUC"),   term1 = list(variable = "vTechNewCap"),   rhs = 0,   defVal = 0 )  # vTechCap is indexed by region, so this ceiling applies region by region. # for.each is the full year x tech grid (expand.grid, not a recycled # data.frame); rhs sets a declining per-region ceiling. The binding effect is # on GAS -- without it the model builds gas out as the flexible VRE backstop; # coal already phases out on economics. A full fossil exit is infeasible here # (must-run nuclear + limited transmission need firm capacity for peak), so the # schedule keeps a backup floor. defVal = Inf leaves 2025 unbound. EARLY_RET <- newConstraint(   name = "EARLY_RET",   eq = "<=",   # scope to 2030+ only: adding the 2025 milestone (even unbound) makes the LP   # infeasible through rhs interpolation.   for.each = expand.grid(year = c(2030, 2040, 2050), tech = c("ECOA", "EGAS"),                          stringsAsFactors = FALSE),   term1 = list(variable = "vTechCap"),   rhs = data.frame(     tech = rep(c("ECOA", "EGAS"), each = 3),     year = rep(c(2030, 2040, 2050), 2),     rhs  = c(12, 10, 8,   7, 6, 5)     # coal & gas ceilings (GW/region), falling   ),   defVal = Inf )

title: TOPIA I: building the model
text: Collect every block base repository, bind region set, calendar horizon get solvable model:
code: repo <- newRepository("topia",   COA, GAS, BIO, NUC, SOL, WIN, HYD, ELC, CO2,          # commodities   SUP_COA, SUP_GAS, SUP_BIO, SUP_NUC,                   # fuel supplies   RES_SOL, RES_WIN, RES_HYD,                            # renewable resources   IMP_COA, IMP_GAS, #EXP_ELC,                            # rest-of-world trade   WSOL, WWIN, WHYD,                                     # weather   ECOA, EGAS, ENUC, ESOL, EWIN, EHYD, EBIO,             # technologies   STG_ELC,                                              # storage   TBD_ELC_W1_W2, TBD_ELC_W2_C1,                         # electricity, region   TBD_COA_WEST_CENTRAL, TBD_GAS_WEST_CENTRAL,           # fuels, zone   DEM_ELC)                                              # demand length(repo); names(repo) summary(repo) hor <- newHorizon(period = 2025:2055, intervals = c(1, 10, 10, 10),                   name = "base") hor@intervals                               # start | mid | end | label mod <- newModel("TOPIA", data = repo, calendar = cal,                 region = regions, horizon = hor, discount = 0.05) # the zone-balanced fuels need the hierarchy: without it the model sees # `WEST`/`CENTRAL` as undeclared regions and refuses to interpolate mod <- setGeoscale(mod, gs_mod) mod

text: R3 kit wires regions bi-directional transmission links (TBD_ELC_*). plot_trade_map() draws network map layout — pass topia$geoscales (honeycomb); 7-region kit shows six links: Electricity generation technology: dispatch representative summer day – generation stacked technology, storage charging zero, demand line (autoplot(scenario) reads solution via getMix(); note getData() aggregates sub-annual values ANNUAL default – pass timeframe = "highest" timeslice-level data):

Compare scenarios compare_scenarios(): overview carries every run’s objective (differences baseline), value tables flag solved variables moved, autoplot() draws comparison charts. full comparative document one report(cmp) call away. Total system cost (objective) scenario, straight overview: (charts can always hand-rolled tidy layer – getData(scl, ...) getMix(scl, ...) accept named scenario lists add scenario column.) carbon tax CO2 cap cut emissions different mechanisms (price vs quantity); renewable target raises cost can even raise CO2 relative carbon price – useful contrast policy discussion.
code: scen_CO2CAP <- interpolate_model(mod, "CO2CAP", um$CO2_CAP) |>       # emissions cap   solve_scenario(echo = FALSE) scen_CTAX <- interpolate_model(mod, "CARBONTAX", um$CT_CO2) |>       # carbon tax   solve_scenario(echo = FALSE) scen_RES <- interpolate_model(mod, "RES_SHARE", um$RES_SHARE) |>     # renewable target   solve_scenario(echo = FALSE) scen_NUC <- interpolate_model(mod, "NO_NEW_NUC", um$NO_NEW_NUC) |>   # no new nuclear   solve_scenario(echo = FALSE) scen_ERET <- interpolate_model(mod, "EARLY_RET", um$EARLY_RET) |>    # early fossil retirement   solve_scenario(echo = FALSE) scl <- list(BASE = scen_BASE, CO2CAP = scen_CO2CAP,             CARBONTAX = scen_CTAX, RES_SHARE = scen_RES,             EARLY_RET = scen_ERET) cmp <- compare_scenarios(scl) cmp autoplot(cmp, "emissions") with(cmp$overview, setNames(round(objective), scenario))

title: TOPIA II: running scenarios
text: levcost() solved scenario returns ex-post levelized cost process: discounted sum costs (annualised investment vTechEac, fixed variable O&M, attributed fuel) divided output solution. reads actual results – mini-model – exact model’s time resolution, calendar caveat. ENUC runs base-year capacity, capital already sunk – annualised-investment term eac ~0 realized cost fixed O&M plus fuel; newly built plant add eac . cost per PJ also depends hard plant run: output spreads fixed costs, lowering levelized cost. Priced across scenarios, ENUC’s LCOE tracks much existing fleet dispatched policy mix changes: (levcost(scen, name) attributes fuel vTechInp, works single-fuel technologies ; plant grouped fuel input need group activity instead.) full technology datasheet ex-post cost embedded one call away (report() renders HTML/PDF; needs pandoc):
code: lc <- levcost(scen_BASE, name = "ENUC")      # the existing nuclear fleet lc$levcost_npv                               # NPV levelized cost, MUSD/PJ autoplot(lc, type = "components")            # eac / fixom / varom / supply, by year sapply(scl, function(s) {   lc <- suppressMessages(levcost(s, name = "ENUC"))   if (inherits(lc, "levcost")) round(as.numeric(lc$levcost_npv), 2) else NA_real_ }) report(scen_BASE, name = "ENUC", format = "html")  # the whole-scenario results report: run provenance (scenario_runs()), # solution checks, generation/capacity charts, and a role-driven cost # breakdown; `run =` reports any recorded run, not only the active one report(scen_BASE)

title: Energy Systems Modeling Toolbox
text: comprehensive, modular energy system modeling framework R interface. energyRt (energy system modeling R-toolbox, /ˈɛnərdʒi ɑrt/) provides modular framework macro-language defining, generating, solving, analyzing energy system optimization models R. Instead writing mathematical equations application, modelers describe system using reusable components: commodities, technologies, supply, demand, storage, trade. energyRt translates descriptions optimization models returns results ready analysis R. Build models reusable components, simple examples large-scale applications. Define system ; adapt analysis question. Temporal resolution, geographical detail, solution strategy, solver backend can change without rebuilding conceptual model. Start compact teaching example, extend detailed sectoral national model, explore alternative spatial temporal representations system.

title: Energy Systems Modeling Toolbox
text: Model system, implementation. Express energy technologies relationships inspectable R objects; let energyRt generate sets, mappings, equations, solver-specific code. Build incrementally reuse components. Assemble complex systems smaller, understandable bricks; update components derive model variants without duplicating entire formulations. Choose right scale question. Combine multiple balancing timeframes nested geographical levels, experiment aggregation sampling without redefining underlying system. Avoid solver lock-. Use MathProg, JuMP, Pyomo, GAMS, experimental direct LP-matrix route, depending computational environment problem size. Go beyond single solve. Manage scenarios, inspect generated models, validate solutions, visualize results, build reproducible analyses. energyRt provides modeling machinery rather fixed model, dataset, scenario. intended analysts, researchers, educators, model developers need flexibility transparency — introductory exercises large-scale energy-system studies.

code: library(energyRt)  GAS <- newCommodity(   name = "GAS",   timeframe = "ANNUAL" ) ELC <- newCommodity(   name = "ELC",   timeframe = "ANNUAL" )  SUP_GAS <- newSupply(   name = "SUP_GAS",   commodity = "GAS",   supply = data.frame(cost = 6.0)         # MEUR/PJ )  EGAS <- newTechnology(   name = "EGAS",   input = list(comm = "GAS"),   output = list(comm = "ELC"),   ceff = data.frame(     comm = "GAS",     cinp2use = 0.55   ),   invcost = list(invcost = 900),          # MEUR/GW   fixom = 25,   cap2act = 31.536,   olife = 25L )  DEM_ELC <- newDemand(   name = "DEM_ELC",   commodity = "ELC",   demand = data.frame(demand = 50)        # PJ/year )  mod <- newModel(   name = "HELLO",   data = newRepository("parts", GAS, ELC, SUP_GAS, EGAS, DEM_ELC),   region = "R1",   discount = 0.05,   horizon = newHorizon(     period = 2025:2040,     intervals = c(1, 5, 10),     mid_is_end = TRUE   ) )  scen <- solve_model(   mod,   name = "BASE",   solver = solver_options$glpk )  getData(scen, "vObjective", merge = TRUE)   # discounted system cost getData(scen, "vTechCap", merge = TRUE)     # installed capacity scen_highs <- solve_model(   mod,   name = "BASE_highs",   solver = solver_options$julia_highs ) scen <- mod |>   interpolate(name = "BASE") |>   solve()

what: Compare interpolation settings (size & build time) for a model — compare_interp_settings
title: Compare interpolation settings (size & build time) for a model — compare_interp_settings
text: Interpolates mod memory several setting combinations tabulates big resulting model : total value-parameter rows, parameter / map / set counts, variable & constraint estimate (model_size()), -memory size, build time. quick way see fold / sparse / prune trade model size speed committing solve.

title: Compare interpolation settings (size & build time) for a model — compare_interp_settings
code: compare_interp_settings(   object,   settings = NULL,   ...,   name = "cmp",   verbose = FALSE,   top_n = 12L,   keep_scen = FALSE )

title: Compare interpolation settings (size & build time) for a model — compare_interp_settings
text: object model. settings named list setting combinations; element list arguments forwarded interpolate_model(), e.g. list(fold = TRUE, sparse = TRUE, prune = TRUE). what: energyRt: Energy Systems Modeling Toolbox — energyRt-package
title: energyRt: Energy Systems Modeling Toolbox — energyRt-package
text: macro-language energy system modeling R. Describe system reusable building blocks (commodities, technologies, supply, demand, storage, trade); energyRt compiles least-cost capacity-expansion dispatch optimization model, solves 'GLPK'/'MathProg', 'Julia'/'JuMP', 'Python'/'Pyomo' 'GAMS', direct LP matrix, returns tidy results. Time resolution, geography solver separate choices, one can change without rewriting model. Built-tools cover structural validation, levelized costs, reports, plotting.

title: Visualize a Calendar object — autoplot.calendar
text: object object class calendar. ... Passed plot_calendar(). fill One "order" (chronology, default), "share" (year-share timeslice), "weight" — metric mapped rectangle fill color. color_pattern fill = "order", color gradient applied: "within" (default) colors level timeslices — full h00→h23 gradient recycled every day, d001→d365 year — row shows cyclical structure; "global" colors absolute chronology (leaf order 1…n, e.g. 0…8760). Ignored "share"/"weight". palette Viridis color option (e.g. "D", "C", "magma") fill scale. labels Logical; draw labels inside rectangles (master /). label_by label rectangle : "name" (default) individual level name (e.g. HOUR cells become h00…h23, YDAY cells d001…d365), "timeslice" full timeslice path (e.g. d001_h00), "none". label_color Text color labels. "auto" (default) contrasts label cell — white darker part gradient, dark lighter part — labels stay readable dark fills. Pass single color (e.g. "black", "white") use labels. max_labels Integer; timeframes timeslices left unlabeled avoid clutter. border Rectangle outline color. NA (default) draws outline, high-resolution row (e.g. 8760 hourly timeslices) reads smooth gradient instead solid block borders. Pass e.g. "grey30" outline timeslices coarse calendars. show_leafs Select timeslices draw (NULL, default, shows ). Two forms: unnamed vector filtering finest (leaf) level — leaf timeslice names (e.g. "d001_h05") integer leaf indices (e.g. 1:100 first 100 leaves); named list filtering per timeframe level, combined , e.g. list(YDAY = "d100", HOUR = 5:10) — level character vector level's timeslice names integer positions among timeslices (HOUR = 5:10 selects 5th–10th hours). kept timeslices packed left--right x-axis spans total year-share. Colors stay stable (e.g. h05 keeps color whether hours shown). reference Optional full calendar. supplied, x treated subset reference: plot lays reference's full structure fills timeslices present x (matched timeslice name), leaving unselected timeslices empty. title: Generate a summary report for an energyRt object — report
text: object energyRt S4 object: technology, repository, model, solved scenario. template Character.  Template name defines parameters display.  Currently "generic" built package.  Pass absolute path custom .Rmd file use template. Default NULL selects "generic" automatically. image_file Character.  Optional path PNG/JPG image displayed upper-right corner page.  Defaults object's misc$image names existing local file (see object_image); NULL misc$image skips image. file Character.  Destination file path (used verbatim).  Without report lands inside owning folder's reports/ object saved (scenario folder, model/repository store entry), otherwise temporary project-level get_reports_path() folder. format Character.  Output format: "html" (default), "pdf", "tex" (standalone LaTeX source), "docx" (Word; templates' LaTeX styling degrades Word's styles). Multiple values accepted; one file produced per format. "pdf"/"tex" require LaTeX installation (e.g. tinytex::install_tinytex()) skipped warning none found. levcost levcost (levcost_list) object returned levcost, NULL (default).  NULL levcost keyword arguments passed via ... (e.g. group, repo, discount), levcost() called automatically object arguments. whole-model scenario report, levcost = TRUE adds levelized-cost comparison section (overall per-topology-group charts + table). process declaring vintages clusters report carries per-variant levelised costs (table plus comparison chart) alongside detail figures one display instance. Pass by_variant = FALSE ... report single instance . by_variant consumed report() deliberately forwarded levcost(), whose by_variant = TRUE returns extracted data frame rather object report built . cost_unit Character NULL.  Cost unit label used LCOE axis (e.g. "USD/GJ").  NULL derives label object@units. open Logical.  Open rendered report system browser/viewer done.  Defaults interactive() (opens interactive session, stays quiet scripts knits). ... Arguments forwarded levcost (levcost = NULL levcost parameters provided) /rmarkdown::render().  Known levcost parameter names intercepted automatically; everything else passed renderer. whole-scenario report, levcost = TRUE adds ex-post levelized-cost table via levcost(scenario). levcost_peers levcost_list process's topology-group peers, rendered comparison chart. Filled automatically datasheet requested container (report(mod, name = )); rarely passed hand. geoscale geoscales::GeoScale (technology / storage methods), giving report geometry can map process declared. Nothing costs changes. model model process sits (technology / storage methods). levelized cost computed model's world – calendar, horizon, discount regions – model's geoscale supplies map. scenario solved scenario (technology / storage methods): report adds solve REALIZED – capacity built per region, ex-post levelized cost beside ex-ante one, per variant. scenario implies model, implies geoscale; model scenario's refused. model method, interpolated scenario (solved ) model: diagnostics – processes operate (process_operability()) – added report. reports_path Character.  Redirects default output directory call (file = still wins). force Logical.  Re-render even existing files date.  Reports skip--current: sidecar (*.report.yml) records content key object, template, arguments, image levcost identity, unchanged report rebuilt. logos Character vector image paths rendered banner row (model / repository / scenario methods). Given explicitly REPLACES misc-derived set entirely every file must exist; NULL (default) takes misc$logos, scalar misc$logo / misc$image – scenario shows model's logos first, . figure optional half-page hero figure (model / repository methods); NULL (default) takes misc$figure. groups Process groups model scenario reports: named list whose elements character vectors process names regular expressions process names (list(Coal = "_coal_", Wind = c("WIN_ON", "^R._win"))). Defaults object@misc$report_groups (scenario falls back model's). FALSE disables groups, "topology" groups automatically structure. Without groups report shows representative sample 12 processes. Processes group form final "Ungrouped" sample. interpolate model method: FALSE (default) adds diagnostics; TRUE interpolates model memory (nothing saved) adds processes operate interpolation's warnings; list passes arguments interpolate_model(), e.g. list(calendars$d365_h24_1dpm). interpolation stops reported section instead failing report. run Character NULL (scenario method). run id report, listed scenario_runs ("<solve>" "<variant>/<solve>").  default NULL reports active run; different run read local copy, caller's scenario keeps active run. verify Logical (scenario method), default TRUE: include verify_solution checks section. badges Small property-indicator images (scenario method); NULL (default) takes misc$badges. Branding content enters render key, changed logo figure re-renders otherwise --date report.

Missing files dropped silently; single image capped half frac_total lone logo span page. report_pagebreak(): Emit page break: always-break <div> HTML (honoured printing), \newpage LaTeX, raw {=openxml} block Word. Call results='asis' chunk. report_fig_height(): Figure height (inches) ggplot's facet layout: base one panel row, per_row every row, capped max. Non-ggplot input returns base. report_plot_png(): Rasterise ggplot dpi return png path (uniform pipeline three formats; avoids knitr fig options, docx partly rejects). h_in = NULL sizes facet layout via report_fig_height(). report_fig(): Emit ggplot report figure: -plot title/subtitle dropped (document names figure), height follows facet layout unless h_in given, caption becomes pandoc figure caption. NULL plots emit nothing. report_sec(): Section divider + bold title (+ gray note); Word gets markdown heading. report_tbl(): One table pipeline: prune empty columns, round numerics, kable per format. kable escaping (single-escaped, never double). Large tables stay readable: HTML table 15 rows renders inside scrollable box sticky header (scroll = FALSE disables); max_rows caps printed rows "... K rows (N)" footer – PDF/Word additionally enforce 200-row safety cap max_rows given. report_css(): Emit shared report stylesheet (HTML ; -op Word LaTeX). report_header(): Page header: name + description left, optional image (logo) right.

title: Create a new
code: ECOAL <- newTechnology(   name = "ECOAL", # name, used in sets, no white spaces or special characters   desc = "Generic coal power plant", # any description of the technology   input = data.frame(     comm = "COAL", # name of input commodity     unit = "MMBtu", # unit of the input commodity     # combustion factor from 0 to 1 (default 1) to calculate emissions     # from fuels combustion (commodities intermediate consumption, more broadly)     combustion = 1   ),   output = data.frame(     comm = "ELC", # name of output commodity     unit = "MWh" # unit of the output commodity   ),   aux = data.frame(     acomm = c("NOx", "SO2", "Hg"), # names of auxilary commodities     unit = c("kg", "kg", "g") # units   ),   # Capacity to activity ration: 8760 MWh output a year per MW of capacity   cap2act = 8760,   ceff = data.frame( # efficiency parameters for the main commodities     comm = "COAL",     # efficiency, 1/10 MWh per MMBtu, inverse heat rate     # check: 1 / convert(10, "MMBtu", "MWh") ~= 34% efficiency     cinp2use = 1 / 10   ),   aeff = data.frame( # paramaters for the auxilary commodities     acomm = c("NOx", "SO2", "Hg"),     act2aout = c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3) # emission factors, linked to activity   ),   af = data.frame( # availability (capacity) factor by time timeslices     af.up = 0.95 # maximum 95% per hour   ),   afs = data.frame( # availability factor by timeframes     timeslice = "ANNUAL", # annual availability factor     afs.lo = 0.40, # at least 40% per year     afs.up = 0.85 # maximum 85% per year   ),   fixom = data.frame( # fixed operational and maintenance cost     region = c("R1", "R2", NA), # regions, NA - all other regions     fixom = c(100, 200, 150) # MW a year   ),   varom = data.frame( # variable operational and maintenance cost     region = c("R1", "R2"), # regions     varom = c(1, 2) # $1 and $2 per MWh   ),   invcost = data.frame( # investment cost     year = c(2020, 2030, 2040), # to differentiate by years     invcost = c(1000, 900, 800) # $1000, $900, $800 per MW   ),   vintage = data.frame( # investment window and operational life     start = 2020, # can be installed from 2020     end = 2040, # can be installed until 2040     olife = 30 # operational life, years   ),   capacity = data.frame( # existing capacity     year = c(2020, 2030, 2040), # to differentiate by years     region = c("R1"), # exists only in R1     stock = c(300, 200, 100) # age-based exogenous retirement   ),   # regions where the technology can be installed   region = c("R1", "R2", "R5", "R7"), ) draw(ECOAL)

title: Synthetic input shapes on a calendar (deterministic) — topia_profile
text: shape "step" (ascending staircase levels plateaus: 0, 1/(levels-1), ..., 1), "sine", "cosine", "hex" (trapezoid ramp/plateau/ramp equal thirds). levels integer >= 2, number plateaus shape = "step" (ignored otherwise). levels = 2 /case. calendar calendar object, name shipped calendar (see calendars), timetable data.frame. regions optional character vector. NULL returns bare shape (timeslice, step, value); otherwise shape replicated per region leading region column. vary per-region variation (needs regions): "none" replicates identically; "phase" shifts region (-1)/n period (gradient across map – neighbouring regions peak sequence); "amplitude" scales region 's amplitude 1 - (-1)/(2(n-1)) (1 1/2 – good sites poor sites). min, max numeric range unit shape scaled (value = min + shape * (max - min)). period "year" (one cycle calendar) "frame" (one cycle inside parent timeframe finest level). phase numeric, fraction period shape shifted (applied regions, top vary = "phase" offsets).

Checks: NA index columns: NA parameter's dimSets id columns. fold = TRUE, NA permitted trimmable dimensions (region / timeslice / vintage, fold encodes wildcards); fold = FALSE, NA permitted id column. Parameter vs map (efficiency): value parameter rows lie within union maps (orphan / --domain rows). trimming must hold exactly. Calendar chronology: timeslice successor chain (storage balance ramping order) derived calendar's timetable row order; row order contradicts timetable's timeframe columns structural.
